classification.difficultyReason: Chain two fractional speed changes and infer the inverse time change over a fixed distance, combining fraction arithmetic with the taught rate-time relation.

content.prompt: If Alice can swim 100 m backstroke in 1 minute 20 seconds and she can swim butterfly at $\frac{9}{8}$ times her backstroke speed, and freestyle at $\frac{10}{9}$ times her butterfly speed, how fast can she swim 100 m freestyle?

answer.short:
1 minute 4 seconds.

For the same distance, divide the backstroke time by the combined speed multiplier.
answer.worked:
The backstroke time is $60+20=80$ seconds.

$$\begin{aligned}\text{Freestyle speed multiplier}&=\frac{9}{8}\times\frac{10}{9}\\\text{Freestyle speed multiplier}&=\frac{5}{4}\end{aligned}$$

For a fixed distance, time is divided by the speed multiplier.

$$\begin{aligned}\text{Freestyle time}&=80\div\frac{5}{4}\\\text{Freestyle time}&=80\times\frac{4}{5}\\\text{Freestyle time}&=64\text{ seconds}\end{aligned}$$

Alice can swim 100 m freestyle in 1 minute 4 seconds.
